verification_report.summary: The complete proof passes sequential verification under the explicitly stated real-polyhedral conventions. The slope lemma correctly translates incident-face Jensen inequalities into ray convexity and all nonnegative balancing relations. For the one-vertex theorem, positivity of the balancing vector gives the claimed dimension formula. The local raising perturbations preserve convexity, the obstacle bound, and growth, proving contact at every positive atom when dim K=1. When dim K>1, an extreme relation has proper support; the constructed obstacle has exactly the claimed envelope and a strictly negative orthogonality integral. The bounded-reference-shift identity and the index-two tripod computations are valid. For the graph theorem, refinement preserves rank-one cones, and the star perturbation preserves all local Jensen inequalities, including the cutoff slope jumps. Bounded edges and cycles introduce no further constraint. The trivalent corollary follows because incident rays are distinct in the embedded polyhedral-space setting. External references were queried through search_arxiv_theorems first, then located and checked in [BMPS26](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.08664v1). Proposition 6.13 supports the stated real-affine extension; Definitions 3.1–3.3 and Lemma 3.4 give the relevant convexity characterization; Definition 6.15 and Proposition 6.17 confirm the Laplacian sign and normalization. The literal integral-slope convention was distinguished from the real extension throughout. No critical errors or gaps were found.
